teaching_units.title: Effects of Real Exchange Rate Changes

evidence.quote: When the real exchange rate rises, it is called a real appreciation, meaning domestic goods become more expensive relative to foreign goods.
When the real exchange rate falls, it is called a real depreciation, meaning domestic goods become cheaper relative to foreign goods.
U.S. exports are decreasing as the real exchange rate rises.
